# Monday, November 2nd

Too quiet today. The sea lay flat as a dinner plate all morning, and the gulls were sitting on the rocks instead of wheeling about, which is never a good sign. By breakfast the barometer had dropped four millibars since midnight.

## The barometer

I've been taking readings every two hours since dawn:

| Time  | Pressure (mb) | Notes                         |
|-------|---------------|-------------------------------|
| 06:00 | 1004          | Overcast, wind barely there   |
| 10:00 | 999           | Swell starting from the west  |
| 14:00 | 993           | Gulls gone inland             |
| 18:00 | 987           | First proper gusts            |

Something big is coming in from the northwest, and it's coming in fast.

## No boat

The supply boat was due at eleven. It didn't come. The radio said the mainland harbor master has held everything in port because of the forecast, which is sensible of him and terribly inconvenient for me. That means another week without the spare bearing for the lens motor, and the motor has been making a sound I don't like.

> The old log from 1961 has a margin note in my predecessor's hand: *"When the gulls go quiet, check your shutters."*

I checked my shutters.

**Storm prep:**

- [x] Close and bar the storm shutters
- [x] Fill the spare water cans
- [x] Top up the generator fuel
- [x] Bring the wash line in
- [ ] Tie down the dinghy properly (I ran out of daylight)

## Evening

Soup and the last of the good bread for supper. I read for an hour and then gave up, because I kept listening to the wind instead of the book. The light is turning steadily. I'll go up again before bed and once more around two, if the weather wakes me, and I suspect it will.

Things I'm grateful for today:

1. The generator started first time.
2. The pantry is fuller than I thought.
3. A quiet day to get ready, even if I didn't enjoy it.

Tomorrow: ride it out, and hope that nobody is out on the water in this.

— *M.H.*
